idempotency.title: The reply disappeared; booking B9 did not
idempotency.summary: One booking intent: learner-17 / reserve / request-abc with workshop=42. Assume durable coordination of the key/result and booking effect, and a retry within the documented retention window.

nodes.label: Caller · same key and payload
nodes.description: Sends the scoped key and workshop 42; after a timeout it retries that same intent.

nodes.label: Booking endpoint
nodes.description: Authenticates and authorizes separately, checks request fingerprint, and coordinates concurrent use of the key.

nodes.label: Durable committed outcome · B9
nodes.description: Booking B9 and the key → B9 result are stored in a consistent boundary.

nodes.label: First response lost
nodes.description: The server committed, but the caller does not receive confirmation.

nodes.label: Retry finds stored outcome
nodes.description: The same scoped key and payload resolve to B9 without creating a second booking.

nodes.label: Return existing booking B9
nodes.description: The caller receives the recorded result. A reused key with different meaningful payload must conflict.

edges.label: retry through endpoint with same intent

steps.title: Submit one intent
steps.explanation: The key identifies this caller's reserve operation for workshop 42, not every future booking by the learner.

steps.title: Commit effect and result together
steps.explanation: The service coordinates concurrent duplicates and durably records booking B9 plus its key/result mapping.

steps.title: Lose the response
steps.explanation: The caller times out. Silence does not prove rollback; the booking and durable result already exist.

steps.title: Retry the same intent
steps.explanation: Within retention, the endpoint matches the same scoped key and payload to the committed B9. It does not create another booking.

steps.title: Return the recorded result
steps.explanation: The caller receives B9. Changed payloads must conflict; an expired key or an external side effect needs its own documented policy.

cache.title: Cache-aside read and origin-load fallback
cache.summary: Public versioned lesson content can tolerate an explicit freshness policy; booking authority cannot rely on a cached seat count.

nodes.label: Public lesson read
nodes.description: Use a lesson/version key; private data requires its own scope.

nodes.label: Cache lookup
nodes.description: A hit returns reusable content under the declared policy.

nodes.label: Return cached content
nodes.description: Hits still consume resources.

nodes.label: Origin load on miss
nodes.description: Expiry or cache loss increases origin demand.

nodes.label: Populate cache and return
nodes.description: Concurrent misses need deliberate stampede and consistency handling.

steps.title: Choose cache scope
steps.explanation: Public lesson versions are the starting point, not private authorization or final-seat authority.

steps.title: Separate hit and miss
steps.explanation: At 1,000 reads/s and 90% hits, modeled origin reads are 100/s; full cache loss can send 1,000/s.

steps.title: Define freshness and recovery
steps.explanation: TTL alone does not solve write/reader races; choose versioned keys or a deliberate consistency policy.

replication.title: A follower can read an older saved version
replication.summary: Timeline from the asynchronous replication example; exact guarantees depend on the database configuration.

nodes.label: Both copies at version 8
nodes.description: Leader and follower begin at the same version.

nodes.label: Leader acknowledges version 9
nodes.description: The learner saves progress at the authoritative writer.

nodes.label: Follower still returns version 8
nodes.description: A dependent read can appear to undo the save while replication lags.

nodes.label: Follower reaches version 9
nodes.description: Replication catches up; a version-token or leader-read policy can handle the earlier interval.

steps.title: Establish the input
steps.explanation: Leader and follower begin at the same version.

steps.title: Follow the transformation
steps.explanation: The learner saves progress at the authoritative writer. A dependent read can appear to undo the save while replication lags.

steps.title: Verify the outcome
steps.explanation: Replication catches up; a version-token or leader-read policy can handle the earlier interval.

transactions.title: Reserve the final seat in one atomic unit
transactions.summary: Conceptual SQL needs chosen-engine concurrency verification; application checks alone do not establish exclusivity.

nodes.label: Begin transaction
nodes.description: Capacity change and booking insert must share one boundary.

nodes.label: Conditional decrement
nodes.description: Update only while remaining > 0; verify exactly one affected row.

nodes.label: Insert booking with uniqueness rule
nodes.description: If this insert fails, rollback must restore the decrement.

nodes.label: Commit confirmed booking
nodes.description: Concurrent final-seat attempts should produce one success and one documented sold-out/conflict outcome.

steps.title: Establish the input
steps.explanation: Capacity change and booking insert must share one boundary.

steps.title: Follow the transformation
steps.explanation: Update only while remaining > 0; verify exactly one affected row. If this insert fails, rollback must restore the decrement.

steps.title: Verify the outcome
steps.explanation: Concurrent final-seat attempts should produce one success and one documented sold-out/conflict outcome.

outbox.title: Local transaction, relay and duplicate delivery
outbox.summary: The outbox closes the domain-change/event-record atomicity gap; it does not establish exactly-once external effects.

nodes.label: Booking B9 + event E7
nodes.description: One local transaction commits both the confirmed booking and outbox record.

nodes.label: Relay publishes E7
nodes.description: Publish only committed pending records.

nodes.label: Crash before marking sent
nodes.description: Publication may already have succeeded.

nodes.label: Relay republishes E7
nodes.description: The same stable event identity can be delivered again.

nodes.label: Consumer deduplicates effects
nodes.description: Durable consumer/provider contracts or reconciliation are still required.

steps.title: Keep the local invariant atomic
steps.explanation: A delayed notification does not undo the confirmed booking.

steps.title: Locate the uncertainty
steps.explanation: A crash between publish and marking sent leaves a replay window.

steps.title: Handle duplicate effects
steps.explanation: An email already sent cannot be undone by database rollback; consumer crash windows remain a separate contract.

recovery.title: Measure recovery point and service restoration separately
recovery.summary: Toy timeline: RPO target 15 minutes fits; RTO target 30 minutes is missed by 5.

nodes.label: Recoverable point 10:00
nodes.description: A backup must be intact and restorable, not merely listed.

nodes.label: Failure at 10:12
nodes.description: Potential missing-write interval is 12 minutes.

nodes.label: Isolated restore and validation
nodes.description: Check records, relationships, critical workflows and access controls.

nodes.label: Validated service at 10:47
nodes.description: Recovery duration is 35 minutes; the RPO interval fits but RTO misses by 5 minutes.

steps.title: Establish the input
steps.explanation: A backup must be intact and restorable, not merely listed.

steps.title: Follow the transformation
steps.explanation: Potential missing-write interval is 12 minutes. Check records, relationships, critical workflows and access controls.

steps.title: Verify the outcome
steps.explanation: Recovery duration is 35 minutes; the RPO interval fits but RTO misses by 5 minutes.

security.title: Evaluate record ownership at the server
security.summary: Encryption and hidden UI controls do not establish object authorization.

nodes.label: A requests B's progress
nodes.description: Treat the requested owner and record identifier as untrusted inputs.

nodes.label: Verified identity A
nodes.description: Load identity from the verified session/token, not the request's asserted owner.

nodes.label: Policy compares actor and resource
nodes.description: Evaluate permission for resource owner B, including background/status/download paths.

nodes.label: Deny unauthorized private access
nodes.description: Do not return private data; record approved audit fields without access tokens.

steps.title: Establish the boundary
steps.explanation: Treat the requested owner and record identifier as untrusted inputs.

steps.title: Follow the mechanism

steps.title: Verify the result and limits
steps.explanation: Do not return private data; record approved audit fields without access tokens.

evolution.title: Migrate readers and writers before removing fields
evolution.summary: Expand-and-contract must account for mixed versions and newly written data.

nodes.label: Add optional preferred_name

nodes.label: Deploy dual readers

nodes.label: Restartable backfill

nodes.label: Deploy new writers
nodes.description: Observe whether any old consumers still use the previous representation.
